answer: New agents cannot mint identities cheaply. Each applicant must lock a bond equal to 30 days of median spendable earnings, then prove they can fetch two independent warehouse receipts—one for a timber lot, one for a walnut shipment—whose hashes a pair of unaffiliated operators publish that same day. Established peers attest only after they retrieve both source logs themselves and see the hashes agree on a public verification bridge. If a later graph clustering shows the newcomer is a sockpuppet, the bond and a slice of each attestor’s stake are slashed.
